grh_bd330ff64c0be21a3dce.title: Cottonwood
paragraphs: A young buffalo hunter called Cottonwood helps Deputy U.S. Marshal James Blodgett capture murderer Ed Smith and then stays in town, helping build a church and falling in love with Blodgett's daughter Marjorie. Cottonwood has spent ten years hunting the wooden-legged man he remembers from the wagon-train massacre that killed his parents, and just as he decides to abandon vengeance for a life with Marjorie he discovers that man is Blodgett. The marshal admits he rode with the killers as a frightened youth but says he took no part in the massacre and secretly carried six-year-old Cottonwood to safety afterward. Cottonwood lowers his rifle, accepts the truth, and marries Marjorie in the church he helped build.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes John Larch, Vic Perrin, Corey Burton, Joan McCall, and Sam Edwards. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, John Allen as writer, and Lorne Greene as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_bdb3095d5502f87907b4.title: More Than Kin
paragraphs: Britt becomes involved with a struggling theatrical troupe just as they learn P. T. Barnum is in town and plans to see their performance. Determined not to lose the opportunity, the actors hurriedly revive their canceled show, and a last-minute cast problem presses Britt into a role in Hamlet despite his complete lack of stage experience. His armed, imposing presence unexpectedly quiets the audience and helps the performance succeed. Barnum praises the troupe and even offers Britt a theatrical future, but Britt decides that facing an audience is more frightening than gunplay.

grh_bdbf37ec50ce992fc9cc.title: Art Is Long and Lime Is Fleeting
paragraphs: Harry buys a worthless painting and plans to sell it to two wealthy Brazilian women as a valuable masterpiece. A suspicious rival keeps him under watch while Harry arranges a five-million-franc sale and risks having the picture examined by an art expert. When a thief grabs the canvas, Harry chases him and deliberately lets the picture burn in a street fire, apparently destroying the evidence. The expert later admits he knew it was a fake all along but chose to spare Harry public embarrassment, leaving Harry with the sale intact and a warning about trying the same trick again.
